short_answer: Sean Murphy is a real, active pick seller. On 17 Nov 2026 PickDawgz listed his plays through 16 Nov 2026, and Capper Reviews and SportsCapping, both part of the SportsCapping network, listed his packages. We found no store or company of his own. His bio says he began as lead handicapper for Pat Miller Sports in 2003; that service did exist and sold picks through Covers, but the saved pages we opened do not name him.

PickDawgz posts his full graded pick history, which lets anyone check the sales claims. We counted the 1,456 graded picks from 17 Nov 2025 to 16 Nov 2026: 738 wins, 706 losses and 12 pushes, 51.1% winners, about 22.7 units down when each pick risks one unit at the posted odds. College football was his best sport (77-58, about 9 units up); hockey and baseball lost the most.

The hot runs in his package titles are real but chosen. The 17-3-1 college football run matches his last 21 college football picks exactly; go back four more picks and it becomes 18-6-1. The PickDawgz last 30 days table showed only his three winning leagues and left out the four that lost units.
Independent buyer talk is almost absent: three favorable comments on a network owned site, and a forum that bars members from reposting his plays. We found no complaints about billing or refunds.

guarantee: PickDawgz says that when a "Credit Guaranteed" package does not profit, "a credit for its full purchase price is automatically issued," and that credits "expire 9 months after they are added to your account." It is store credit, not cash, and the passes showed no guarantee wording. The PickDawgz terms add: "All sales are final regardless of the duration of membership access."

SportsCapping's current Profit Guarantee page says a guaranteed package that finishes at zero profit or less ("breaking even counts") earns the handicapper's next day of picks free, a guaranteed subscription is extended by its original length, some accounts get account credit instead, "Season and rest-of-season passes are not guaranteed," and "Guarantees apply once per purchase."

The older policy page on Capper Reviews, part of the same network, words it differently: free time equal to what you bought if a package loses a single unit, grading on 100 unit intervals, one free period per purchase, "There is NO GUARANTEE on seasonal subscriptions," and "We do not offer a money back policy like some services do."
None of these versions refunds cash or covers your losses on the bets themselves.

claims_note: How we counted: PickDawgz shows every graded pick with the line and odds. We read 155 pages of his history on 17 Nov 2026, 1,550 picks from 31 Oct 2025 to 16 Nov 2026, and kept the 12 months from 17 Nov 2025. We scored each pick as risking one unit at the odds shown; 32 winners showed no odds and were scored at -110. PickDawgz may size plays differently, so its own unit totals can differ a little from ours.

12 months by sport, from his own history: college football 77-58-2 (+12.1 units), NFL 60-50 (+5.7), WNBA 69-65 (+4.1), college basketball 140-125-4 (+2.7), NBA 148-132-3 (+2.3), CFL 21-17 (+2.0), MLB 124-138-3 (-21.1), NHL 77-94 (-26.4) and World Cup soccer 13-20 (-5.4). Plays titled 10*, his top rated releases, went 243-247-4, about 24.4 units down.

By month, 6 of the 13 months were down. His last 30 days (18 Oct to 16 Nov 2026) were 80-65-2, about 7.5 units up, so his current form is good, and the SportsCapping leaderboard showed a near identical 80-64-2 for him over its last 30 days.

The college football side run of 351-272 is about 56.3% winners and the totals run of 294-243 about 54.7%. The all time network figure of 694-576-22 is 54.7%. College football is the one sport where every source we checked agrees he has been profitable.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: no third party log. We found no outside tracker, contest record, court case or regulator action about him.

What the sellers publish, and what it shows: PickDawgz posts his complete graded pick history, which is more than most storefronts do. Our count of the last 12 months of it is 738-706-12, 51.1% winners and about 22.7 units down at one unit a pick. At -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

The SportsCapping leaderboard, kept by the network that sells him, showed him 694-576-22 all time in college football, 54-35-2 in college football this season, and 172-154-3 across all sports over the last 90 days. SportsCapping's own method note says a "Best Run" or "since" figure is "a window starting on the date shown, not a lifetime record."

Background: his bio says he worked with The Miller Group from 2006 through 2009 and founded his own service in September 2009, and that he holds a business degree in finance. PickDawgz and SportsChatPlace are owned and run by Dawn Patrol LLC; SportsCapping says it has been "a trusted name in the sports handicapping industry since 2003," and Capper Reviews says it is part of the SportsCapping network.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Sean Murphy is close to nil. The only buyer comments we found sit on a site that says it is part of the network selling his picks. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found almost no buyer talk about Sean Murphy outside the sites that sell him. Capper Reviews, a network owned site, has three undated comments, all favorable, praising his recent results, a long winning history and detailed free pick write ups. TheRX has barred members from reposting his paid plays since at least 2023 and repeated the rule in November 2026, which reflects its policy on paid plays, not his results. Reddit archive searches for his name returned only posts about the baseball catcher of the same name or other people, and our saved copy of ten betting subreddits had nothing on the handicapper. The BBB has no listing for PickDawgz. We found no complaints about billing or refunds, and no independent record either way, so the closest thing to an outside check is our own count of the history PickDawgz posts.

Capper Reviews shows a rating of 3.73 out of 5 from 22 votes and three undated comments. One calls him the best in the business over the past year, one says he has always been a winner and was among the best on Covers a decade ago, and one praises his free picks and the detail of his reasoning. The page says he sells through the SportsCapping network, which Capper Reviews is part of, so this is not independent evidence.

TheRX service play guidelines, posted by forum staff, name Sean Murphy in a list of paid services that members should not post in the service play threads. The rule reflects the forum's policy on paid plays, not a judgment of his results.

The same do not post list was repeated by forum staff at the top of the Saturday service play thread for 14 Nov 2026, still naming Sean Murphy. No member post in that thread discussed his picks or results.

Reddit archive searches for Sean Murphy in r/sportsbetting, r/sportsbook and r/SportsBettingPicks returned only posts about the MLB catcher Sean Murphy or other people with the same surname. Our web searches found no Sportsbook Review or Covers thread reviewing the handicapper.
A BBB search for PickDawgz returned no business, so there is no BBB complaint history for the main storefront that sells him.

conflicts: Capper Reviews, which hosts the star rating and comments, says it is part of the SportsCapping network that sells his packages, and its purchase links carry affiliate codes.
The Capper Reviews page carried a "$1,000 Free Play at MyBookie" banner linked through an affiliate tracking address. MyBookie is an offshore sportsbook, not licensed by U.S. state regulators.
PickDawgz, which grades his picks and builds his record table, also sells his packages. Its last 30 days table showed only the leagues where he was up.
SportsCapping's About page says "No cherry-picked highlights," while the package titles it sells lead with runs whose start dates are chosen.
strengths: A named handicapper with a stated history back to 2003 and an active 2026 card across many sports.
PickDawgz posts his full graded pick history with lines and odds, so buyers can check claims themselves.
Where we checked his advertised hot runs against that history, the numbers were accurate for the windows given.
College football has been profitable in every source we checked: 77-58-2 over 12 months by our count and 694-576-22 all time on the network leaderboard.
Prices are published for every package on both storefronts, and every play comes with a written analysis.
concerns: Over the last 12 months of his own posted history he was 51.1% winners and about 22.7 units down at one unit a pick; his top rated 10* plays did worse.
The PickDawgz last 30 days table showed his three winning leagues and left out four losing ones.
Bio figures of 55% and 57% winners, and a start year of 2003 or 2004, differ between storefronts.
The same passes cost different amounts on the two storefronts.
Guarantees pay in store credit or free time, never cash; season passes have no guarantee, and PickDawgz sales are final.
The main rating page is owned by the selling network and carries an offshore sportsbook affiliate banner.
checklist: Open his PickDawgz pick history and count the last few hundred picks yourself, losses included, before you buy.
Ignore runs in package titles. Check where each run starts; a few picks earlier the record is usually much less shiny.
If you follow him, weigh college football more than hockey or baseball, where his own posted history lost the most over the last year.
Count units, not wins. Totals at the wrong number can turn a winning record into a loss.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Here every version is store credit or free time, and season passes have none.
Compare storefronts before paying. The one year pass was $1,899.95 on one site and $1,999.95 on another.
faq: He is a real, active handicapper whose packages have published prices on established storefronts, and one of them posts his full graded pick history. That history does not show a winning last 12 months overall: we counted 738-706-12, about 22.7 units down. We found no court or regulator action involving him.

His bio says he started as lead handicapper for Pat Miller Sports in 2003, worked with The Miller Group from 2006 to 2009 and has run his own service since September 2009. He is known for totals. Pat Miller Sports did exist and sold through Covers, but we could not find his name on its saved pages.
How much does Sean Murphy cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 single plays were $40 to $50 on PickDawgz, a 30 day pass was $379.95 there and $374.95 on Capper Reviews, a one year pass was $1,899.95 or $1,999.95 depending on the site, and season passes ran $319.95 to $779.95.

No cash refunds. PickDawgz gives store credit on plays marked Credit Guaranteed, credits expire after 9 months, and all sales are final. SportsCapping gives free replacement picks or time, and season passes carry no guarantee.
Does Sean Murphy have a verified record?

No third party record. PickDawgz posts his graded history, and our count of its last 12 months is 51.1% winners. The bigger runs in his package titles, such as 351-272 on college football sides, start on dates the seller chose.

His posted history shows real strength in college football and recent good form, but across all sports over the last year it was a small loss at one unit a pick. Nothing refunds your betting losses, so if you buy, focus on the sport where his own record is strongest and log every pick.
